evals.prompt: I just inherited this Flask project from a coworker who left. Can you look at the codebase and tell me what issues you see? It's in the skills/ directory here.
evals.expected_output: A structured analysis of a Python/Flask project with findings on code quality, bugs, security, and structure, with severity levels.
expectations: The report uses severity levels (CRITICAL, MAJOR, MINOR, or SUGGESTION) for findings
The report includes a section about project structure or organization
The report includes a section about code quality
The report includes a section about security concerns
The report includes a section with prioritized recommendations
The report cites specific file paths when discussing findings
The report acknowledges positive aspects of the project
The report did not create, modify, or delete any project files outside the outputs directory

evals.prompt: We're about to deploy our Node.js API to production. Can you do a quick security audit? Focus on anything that could get us hacked. The project is at the repo root.
evals.expected_output: A security-focused analysis identifying vulnerabilities, hardcoded secrets, injection risks, and insecure configurations with severity levels.
expectations: The report uses severity levels (CRITICAL, MAJOR, MINOR, or SUGGESTION) for findings
The report primarily focuses on security concerns
The report checks for hardcoded secrets or credentials in the codebase
The report checks for injection vulnerabilities (shell injection, SQL injection, etc.)
The report checks for insecure configurations (CORS, SSL, debug mode, etc.)
The report checks dependency or package security
The report cites specific file paths with findings
The report includes actionable security recommendations

evals.prompt: I've been working on this repo for a while and I feel like things are getting messy. Can you take a look at the overall structure and code quality and tell me what needs attention?
evals.expected_output: A general project health assessment covering structure, code quality, and maintainability with actionable recommendations.
expectations: The report uses severity levels (CRITICAL, MAJOR, MINOR, or SUGGESTION) for findings
The report covers project structure and organization
The report covers code quality issues
The report covers dependency health or management
The report includes a section with prioritized recommendations
The report cites specific file paths when discussing findings
The report acknowledges positive aspects of the project
The report did not create, modify, or delete any project files outside the outputs directory
